diagnostic_evidence.quote: $$V^{(\varepsilon)}(t, \cdot) = V(0,\cdot),~\text{for}~ t \in[0,\varepsilon/2],~~ V^{(\varepsilon)}(t, \cdot) = V(t, \cdot),~\text{for}~t \ge \varepsilon,$$ and linear in between $$ V^{(\varepsilon)}(t, \cdot) =\Big(1-\frac{t-(\varepsilon/2)}{\varepsilon/2}\Big)V(0, \cdot) + \frac{t-(\varepsilon/2)}{\varepsilon/2}  V(\varepsilon, \cdot),~~~t \in [\varepsilon/2, \varepsilon].$$

issues.failure_explanation: The construction is constant on $[0,\varepsilon/2]$, then linear on $[\varepsilon/2,\varepsilon]$. At $t=\varepsilon/2$ the left derivative is $0$, while the right derivative is $2(V(\varepsilon)-V(0))/\varepsilon$, which is generally nonzero. At $t=\varepsilon$ the left derivative is $2(V(\varepsilon)-V(0))/\varepsilon$, while the right derivative is $V'(\varepsilon)$. Hence the interpolant is not $C^1$ at the knots.

failure_location.quote: This function lies again in $C^1([0,T], C^b)$, with norm bounded by at most a constant multiple of $\|V\|_{C^1([0,T], C^b)}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the piecewise linear interpolation by a standard smooth interpolation (e.g. mollify the transition) that agrees with $V(0)$ near $0$ and with $V(t)$ for $t\ge\varepsilon$, preserving the same bounds and the constancy on $[0,\varepsilon/2]$.
issues.overall_effect: The regularity assumption on $V^{(\varepsilon)}$ used in Proposition \ref{cstpert} and downstream in Lemma \ref{epsapp} and Theorem \ref{raf} is not justified by the stated construction.
issues.title: Piecewise linear interpolant claimed to be C^1
issues.why_classification: The defect is local and can be fixed by a standard smoothing argument without changing any substantive estimate or conclusion.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
C) [Linear approximation:] There exist a continuous linear operator 
$$\mathbb I_{\theta_0} \equiv D\G_{\theta_0} : L^2(\Omega) \to L^2([0,T], L^2(\Omega))$$
and $1 \le \bar \gamma \le \gamma-d/2, c'>0, c=c(\theta_0, B)>0,$ such that for all $h \in U(\bar \gamma, B), B>0,$ with $\|h\|_{L^2} \le c'$ we have $$\|\G(\theta_0+h) - \G(\theta_0) - \mathbb I_{\theta_0}[h]\|_{L^2([0,T], L^2(\Omega))} \le c \|h\|^2_{L^2(\Omega)}.$$

Writing $\beta = \min(\kappa, \bar \gamma)-\zeta$, straightforward calculations show that the first term in the preceding maximum is of order
$$\sqrt N \int_0^{\sigma_N} u^{-d/2\beta}du \lesssim \sqrt N \tilde \delta_N^{2- d/\beta}(\zeta)$$

issues.failure_explanation: The function $g_{\theta,\psi}$ is the second-order remainder $\G(\theta')-\G(\theta_0)-D\G_{\theta_0}[\theta'-\theta_0]$, which Condition \ref{gemol}C bounds quadratically, not linearly. The proof instead invokes Condition \ref{gemol}B, which only gives a linear bound on the remainder. With the stated linear variance bound $\sigma_N^2 \asymp \tilde\delta_N^2(\zeta)$, the first empirical-process term behaves as $\sqrt N\,\tilde\delta_N^{1-d/(2\beta)}(\zeta)$, not as the claimed $\sqrt N\,\tilde\delta_N^{2-d/\beta}(\zeta)$; the latter corresponds to a quadratic variance $\sigma_N^2 \asymp \tilde\delta_N^4(0)$. Thus the displayed variance bound and the subsequent order calculation are inconsistent, and the claimed $o(1)$ bound for the first empirical process does not follow as written.

failure_location.quote:
By Condition \ref{gemol}B and $L^2 \to L^2([0,T], L^2)$-continuity of $\mathbb I_{\theta_0}$, we can bound the `weak variances' uniformly in $\psi, \theta$ as
$$Ef_{\theta, \psi}^2(Z) \le C \big\| \theta - \theta_0 - \frac{t}{\sqrt N} p_N(\bar \psi_{\theta_0}) \big\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2 \lesssim \tilde \delta^2_N(\zeta) + \frac{1}{N}  \equiv \sigma_N^2,$$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the empirical-process variance bound using Condition \ref{gemol}C (quadratic remainder) and then re-optimize the two terms in the Bernstein/Dudley bound, or supply an alternative chaining argument that handles the small-variance regime; the variance definition $\sigma_N^2$ and the subsequent exponent calculation must be made consistent.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Lemma \ref{oldtimer} is invalid as written, so the Laplace-transform approximation in Theorem \ref{laplaceapp}, the Wasserstein convergence in Proposition \ref{prop:added-1}, and the Bernstein-von Mises theorems that depend on them become unsupported by the given argument.
issues.title: Incorrect variance bound in Lemma oldtimer
issues.why_classification: The defect is contained in a key technical lemma, but repairing it requires a nontrivial reworking of the empirical-process estimate rather than a simple typo correction; the main theorem architecture may survive after such a fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: To prove Theorem \ref{ganzwien}, recall from (\ref{wassdef}) that the Wasserstein distance $\mathscr W_1(\mu, \nu)$  involves suprema over $1$-Lipschitz functions $F: \mathscr C \to \R$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof in Section 3.3 only establishes the Wasserstein convergence of the posterior fluctuations $\sqrt N(u_\theta-u_{\tilde\theta_N})$ to the limiting Gaussian law $\mu$. It never proves the separate convergence in distribution of the centered posterior mean sequence $\sqrt N(u_{\tilde\theta_N}-u_{\theta_0})$ to $\mu$. This second conclusion does not follow from the first and requires an additional linearization argument for the posterior mean.

failure_location.quote:
as well as
$$\sqrt N (u_{\tilde \theta_N} - u_{\theta_0}) \to_{\mathscr C}^d \mu.$$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing argument: use the second part of Theorem \ref{mainbvm} (or the corresponding center convergence) together with the continuous linearization $Du_{\theta_0}$ and the posterior-mean rate to show that the nonlinear remainder $\sqrt N(u_{\tilde\theta_N}-u_{\theta_0}-Du_{\theta_0}[\tilde\theta_N-\theta_0])$ is $o_P(1)$ in $\mathscr C$, then apply the continuous mapping theorem.
issues.overall_effect: The second main conclusion of Theorem \ref{ganzwien} is stated but not proved in the given source.
issues.title: Missing proof of the posterior-mean convergence in Theorem ganzwien
issues.why_classification: The missing step is a short, standard linearization argument that uses already established ingredients and does not affect the validity of the first conclusion.
